relationships.subject: NRP1-4
relationships.evidence_quote: NRP1–4 inhibited the NRP1/VEGF-A interaction with an IC50 of 0.598 nM compared to an IC50 of 930 nM for EG00229 in a cell-free assay

relationships.subject: VEGF-A
relationships.evidence_quote: VEGF-A significantly potentiates neuronal excitability in primary sensory neurons and that this enhancement can be blocked by co-treatment with NRP1–4

relationships.subject: VEGF-A
relationships.evidence_quote: When probing the expression of NaV1.7 we also found that the normalized surface expression of this channel was increased by VEGF-A

relationships.subject: VEGF-A
relationships.evidence_quote: we found that VEGF-A significantly enhanced the expression of CaV2.2 compared to control

relationships.subject: Protox-II
relationships.evidence_quote: Co-application of the NaV1.7 inhibitor PrTx-II abolished the potentiation that was previously observed by VEGF-A

relationships.subject: VEGF-A
relationships.evidence_quote: Acute perfusion with VEGF-A (4 nM) in the external bath solution increased sEPSC frequency compared with control slices

relationships.subject: NRP1-4
relationships.evidence_quote: In rats with spared nerve injury-induced neuropathic pain, intrathecal administration of NRP1-4 significantly attenuated mechanical allodynia.

relationships.subject: NRP1-4
relationships.evidence_quote: Intravenous treatment with NRP1-4 reversed both mechanical allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia in rats with L5/L6 spinal nerve ligation-induced neuropathic pain.

key_findings: VEGF-A increases DRG neuron excitability, Nav1.7 and Cav2.2 currents and membrane expression via NRP1; the VEGF-A sodium current increase is entirely Nav1.7-mediated.
The small-molecule NRP1-4 blocks VEGF-A/NRP1 binding and reverses mechanical allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia in SNI and SNL rats.
